description: Snug main window. C2 note (AC7): capabilities are scoped to the top-level main window ONLY — the sandboxed app iframes must never reach the IPC bridge; the in-shell hard gate asserts unreachability from inside a srcdoc iframe. HTTP scope note (TASK-20261008-p0-clearance W3; ADR-0021 D4 note + §4 amendment): this scope is the BELT for connected-fetch, whose real ceiling is the frozen per-connection allowlist — but it is the ONLY port/loopback limit for the platform-fetch callers outside connected-fetch's scheme and host-class gates (OAuth token/refresh/revoke, the local-model adapter, BYOK, discovery, the relay, release notes, the Ollama probe). https is admitted to any host on ANY port (R-14: a port is not part of a host's identity) and DENIED to loopback (localhost and its subdomains, 127/8), 0/8 and every IPv6 literal. Plain http is admitted only to the three RFC-1918 ranges, written as exact-octet REGEX hosts (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16): the old star form (`http://192.168.*.*:*`) never matched an address — urlpattern IPv4-parses fixed hostname digits, so it compiled to the host `192.0.0.168*.*` — and src-tauri/src/http_scope.rs now tests what the scope ADMITS with the plugin's own matcher. Plus the single Ollama probe port on loopback and the debug-gate stub port. Blanket `http://localhost:*` and `http://127.0.0.1:*` are deliberately absent — connected-fetch refuses loopback outright, so nothing legitimate needs them. The two loopback entries are single-purpose: 11434 is the Ollama probe (threat-model delta §3.5, an accepted residual outside the connected-fetch guards), and 43120 is DEBUG-ONLY — the in-shell gate's net-stub target (gate/run-gate.mjs SNUG_GATE_STUB_PORT). Tauri bakes capability scopes at build time, so the gate's port cannot be added conditionally at runtime; it is admitted here permanently and is inert in a release build, where the debug-only host remap that points at it does not exist (net-remap.ts). Overriding SNUG_GATE_STUB_PORT to a different port requires adding that port here too.
